source: Enterprise Singapore, FAQ: EDGE Grant (SME definition), read 10 Oct 2026; same test on the Enterprise Financing Scheme pages and in SingStat's glossary
rule: A business is an SME if its GROUP annual sales turnover is not more than S$100 million OR its GROUP employment is not more than 200 workers. Meeting EITHER test is enough; it is a non-SME only if it exceeds BOTH. There is one SME tier: Singapore publishes no official micro/small/medium split. Separately, most Enterprise Singapore grants and loans require at least 30% local (Singapore Citizen/PR) ownership; that is an eligibility condition, not part of the size test.

all_sectors.note: One definition for every sector, including F&B, retail and manufacturing. The *_rm keys hold SGD (pack convention, see markets/README.md).

algorithm: group_sales = annual sales turnover of the whole group; group_employees = headcount of the whole group (see group_definition)
do NOT derive micro/small/medium: there is no official tier below SME
report headroom to each limit, then apply scheme-specific overlays (eligibility_overlays) separately: local ownership >= 30%, scheme turnover caps, scheme support levels for SME vs non-SME
group_definition: The group refers to all companies that own more than 50% of the applicant company, as well as all companies that the applicant company owns more than 50% of (EDGE FAQ). The EFS pages define the borrower group more widely: corporate shareholders holding more than 50% at all levels up, subsidiaries more than 50% owned at all levels down, and subsidiaries of the ultimate parent more than 50% owned.

local_ownership.rule: At least 30% held directly or indirectly by Singapore Citizens and/or PRs, determined by ultimate individual ownership

scheme_turnover_caps.ESG-EEG: Group annual sales turnover no more than S$500 million (SME status only decides 70% vs 30% support)
scheme_turnover_caps.ESG-EFS-WCL: Group annual sales turnover not exceeding S$500 million
scheme_turnover_caps.ESG-EFS-FA: Group annual sales turnover not exceeding S$500 million

support_level_by_size.ESG-EDGE: SMEs up to 50% (up to 70% for internationalisation and sustainability activities); non-SMEs up to 30% (50%)
support_level_by_size.ESG-EEG: Base tier: SMEs up to 70%, non-SMEs up to 30%, until 31 Mar 2027

eligibility_overlays.iras_sme_cash_grant_2026: Uses its own test, not the group test: annual revenue no more than S$100 million for YA 2025 (filed and assessed by IRAS as at 31 Aug 2026) OR no more than 200 employees as at 30 Jun 2026

employee_definition: Not defined for the SME test in the cited sources (no full-time/part-time rule is published). Scheme rules differ: the SME Cash Grant counts only 'local qualifying employees' (Singapore Citizens/PRs with on-time CPF contributions); sole proprietors and partners are not employees.

other_sources.what: SingStat glossary: SMEs have operating revenue not more than $100mil or employment not more than 200 workers; non-SMEs exceed both
EFS SME Working Capital: an SME has Group revenue up to S$100 million or a maximum employment size of 200
